governing_thought: Engineering is divided by the kind of system the engineer designs: materials and the making of things, structures, machines and vehicles, energy and process systems, and electrical, information and control systems.
rank_note: Ordered from the matter artefacts are made of, through mechanical and energy systems, to systems that carry information.

pillars.title: Materials and manufacturing
pillars.statement: Materials and manufacturing systems are designed to make artefacts: material classes, nanostructures, fabrication and production processes.

pillars.title: Structures, machines and vehicles
pillars.statement: Structures, machines and vehicles are designed systems whose behaviour is set by force and motion, from aircraft and ships to mechanisms and precision devices.

pillars.title: Energy, fluid and process systems
pillars.statement: Energy, fluid and process systems are designed to convert energy or move and transform matter, as in power plants, heat systems, chemical and environmental processes and resource extraction.

pillars.title: Electrical, information and control systems
pillars.statement: Electrical, information and control systems are designed to carry charge, signals and decisions, from circuits and electromagnetics to communications, sensing, robotics and control.

method_line.title: Method line
method_line.covers: engineering education, design methodology and professional practice
